answer: For a poll on a saffron lantern damaged by a gale, the server rejects malformed rankings of three options. It repeatedly eliminates the lowest first-choice option, transferring ballots to their next choice, until one remains; a tie for elimination ends the poll without a winner. Against 100 identical rankings, their last choice needs 101 contrary ballots to win, costing submission effort. Automation makes this cheap, and ties can halt honest polls.
